title: gemm_bias's mixed_magnitude tolerance is met only by sequential fp32 accumulation, so torch's own matmul fails it and no blocked GEMM on any target can pass

evidence.retained: bw1100 /home/testuser01/oci-dcu-runs/gemm_bias-20260918-064243, four turns and a 400000 token budget, protocol_adherence adhered, endpoint_observation no_qualified_candidate; a CPU-only reproduction on bw1100 using the Workload's own generator and declared tolerance, with no device involved, so the result is hardware-independent
sites: that run's correctness_output: participants.baseline.preflight.launches -- mixed_magnitude passed false, max_abs_error 0.09375, output_mismatches 27, while primary, zeros, near_zero and alternating all pass
the same document's candidate half fails the same case with the same 0.09375, and the run's pooled output_mismatches is 54 -- 27 from each participant
two turns of the same run rejected on correctness with the identical max_abs_error, on different candidate digests
the contrast within the family: gemm_silu's baseline passes every case and only its candidate fails, and gemm's baseline and candidate both pass every case

the declared tolerance_rationale: sized from the measured worst sequential-FP32 departure from an fsum oracle, 3.1e-2 absolute at outputs of order 2e5, and stating 'It is a numerical allowance, not device calibration'

measured on CPU over the mixed_magnitude case: outputs reach absmax 371463, so the allowance at that magnitude is 37.1473 -- but torch's own fp32 matmul departs from an fp64 reference by 0.0596697 with 21 elements outside elementwise tolerance, and a split-K fp32 ordering by 0.0650945 with 22; strictly sequential fp32 departs by 0.0154169 and passes
the same measurement on the primary case: every ordering passes, max departure 3.58e-05

observation:
The baseline is the starter reference the task ships with, and on this target it does not pass the Workload's own validation set. mixed_magnitude is the case it fails -- signed powers of two from 2^-12 to 2^8, so a contraction over K accumulates terms whose magnitudes span twenty binades -- and it fails by 0.09375 on 27 elements while the other four cases pass, primary at 6.87e-05.

That makes gemm_bias unqualifiable on gfx938 by construction. Common Evaluation checks both participants against the external oracle, so a candidate is compared to a reference that is itself outside tolerance; two turns produced two different candidate digests and both were rejected on correctness with the identical error, which is the tell that the error is not the candidate's.

The family separates cleanly and that is what makes this a defect rather than a hard task. gemm's baseline and candidate both pass every case. gemm_silu's baseline passes every case and its candidate fails all five with errors from 0.5 to 100.8 -- a wrong kernel, caught by the oracle, working as intended. Only gemm_bias has a baseline that cannot pass.

What this record does not establish is where the fault sits. A reference that disagrees with torch by 0.09375 at this spread is consistent with an accumulation-order difference the tolerance does not admit, and equally with a tolerance chosen against a different target's arithmetic. Deciding between those needs the same case run on a target whose arithmetic is known to satisfy it, which is not in this evidence.

Resolved, and not where either explanation expected. The question was whether the tolerance was calibrated against arithmetic gfx938 does not have, or the baseline was wrong. Neither: the tolerance is met only by an accumulation order no practical GEMM uses.

Reproduced on CPU with the Workload's own generator and its declared atol and rtol, no device involved, so this is not a property of this target. On mixed_magnitude, torch's own fp32 matmul leaves 21 elements outside the elementwise tolerance and a split-K fp32 ordering leaves 22. Only strictly sequential fp32 passes. On the primary case every ordering passes with room to spare.

The rationale says why, once its own numbers are checked against the case. It sizes the allowance from 'the measured worst sequential-FP32 departure' at 'outputs of order 2e5'. The outputs of this case reach 371463 -- nearly twice that -- and the departure being bounded is the one from sequential accumulation, which is the single order a blocked kernel never uses. The rationale is explicit that it is a numerical allowance rather than device calibration, and that is exactly the trouble: it bounds a quantity no implementation under test produces.

So gemm_bias is unqualifiable on gfx938, on sm_103a, and on anything else that tiles its contraction. That the task was also reported failing on B300 is consistent with this and needs no separate cause.
proposed_change:
The Workload Contract owns this. Two shapes work and the choice is the owner's: size the allowance from the worst departure across the accumulation orders an implementation may actually use -- blocked and split-K, not only sequential -- or narrow mixed_magnitude's exponent range so that a contraction over K keeps its outputs inside the magnitude the current allowance was written for. The rationale should then state which accumulation orders it bounds, since the current one bounds the only order that is never used and says so without noticing.

The B300 comparison this record previously proposed is no longer needed: the reproduction is CPU-only and hardware-independent, so nothing is learned by running it on a second target.

Still do not widen atol to make the case pass. The number to change is the one whose derivation is wrong, and changing it means redoing that derivation against the orders under test -- not raising a threshold until the observed failure fits under it.
